nodes.summary: The Apollonian group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the four matrices $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4$, where $S_i$ agrees with the $4 \times 4$ identity matrix except in row $i$, which has entry $-1$ in column $i$ and entry $2$ in each of the other three columns.
nodes.title: Apollonian group

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a primitive Apollonian circle packing, viewed as an orbit of integral primitive Descartes quadruples. The curvature set of $A$ is the set of all integers that occur as an entry of some quadruple in $A$.
nodes.title: Curvature set

nodes.summary: The Descartes matrix is the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix $M$ with $M_{ii} = 1$ for every $i$ and $M_{ij} = -1$ for $i \ne j$. It is the matrix of the Descartes form: for $v = (a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ one has $v^{\mathsf T} M v = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.
nodes.title: Descartes matrix

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be the set of vectors $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ with $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$. For every matrix $X$ in the Descartes orthogonal group and every $v \in Q$, the vector $Xv$ lies in $Q$, so the Descartes orthogonal group acts on $Q$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.
nodes.title: Descartes orthogonal group action

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be the Descartes matrix. The Descartes orthogonal group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ consisting of the matrices $X$ with $X^{\mathsf T} M X = M$, that is, the invertible integer matrices that preserve the Descartes form $2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.
nodes.title: Descartes orthogonal group

nodes.summary: Call $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ primitive when the greatest common divisor of its four entries is $1$. For every $X \in \mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ and every primitive $v$, the vector $Xv$ is primitive, so $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ acts on the primitive vectors of $\mathbb{Z}^4$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.
nodes.title: General linear group action on primitive vectors

nodes.summary: An integral primitive Descartes quadruple is a vector $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ such that $a + b + c + d > 0$, the Descartes equation $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ holds, and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$.
nodes.title: Integral primitive Descartes quadruple

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a primitive Apollonian circle packing. The missing curvature set of $A$ is the set of positive integers $n$ that do not lie in the curvature set of $A$ but are congruent modulo $24$ to some element of the curvature set of $A$.
nodes.title: Missing curvature set

nodes.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $A$ and a real number $N$, the number of missing curvatures of $A$ up to $N$ is the number of elements $n$ of the missing curvature set of $A$ with $n \le N$, regarded as a real number.
nodes.title: Number of missing curvatures

nodes.summary: A primitive Apollonian circle packing is an orbit of the transformation group acting on the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples.
nodes.title: Primitive Apollonian circle packing

nodes.summary: $S_2$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose second row is $(2, -1, 2, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, 2a - b + 2c + 2d, c, d)$.
nodes.title: The Apollonian generator $S_2$

nodes.summary: $S_3$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose third row is $(2, 2, -1, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, b, 2a + 2b - c + 2d, d)$.
nodes.title: The Apollonian generator $S_3$

nodes.summary: $S_4$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose fourth row is $(2, 2, 2, -1)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, b, c, 2a + 2b + 2c - d)$.
nodes.title: The Apollonian generator $S_4$

nodes.summary: $S_1$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose first row is $(-1, 2, 2, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(-a + 2b + 2c + 2d, b, c, d)$.
nodes.title: The Apollonian generator $S_1$

nodes.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $\mathcal{A}$ and a real number $N$, let $M_{\mathcal{A}}(N)$ be the number of missing curvatures of $\mathcal{A}$ up to $N$. There are infinitely many primitive Apollonian circle packings $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\sqrt{N} = O(M_{\mathcal{A}}(N))$ as $N$ tends to infinity. In other words, for these packings the number of missing curvatures up to $N$ is $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many packings with many missing curvatures

nodes.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the primitive Apollonian circle packing generated by the integral primitive Descartes quadruple $(-3, 5, 8, 8)$. For every integer $n$, $n^2$ does not belong to the curvature set of $\mathcal{A}$.
nodes.title: A packing with no square curvatures

nodes.summary: Each element $g$ of the transformation group sends an integral primitive Descartes quadruple $v$ to $g v$, by matrix–vector multiplication: this is the restriction of the action of the transformation group on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ to the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples, which is closed under the action.
nodes.title: Action of the transformation group on integral primitive Descartes quadruples

nodes.summary: For every $g$ in the transformation group, $g$ maps the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples into itself: if $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ is an integral primitive Descartes quadruple, then so is $g v$.
nodes.title: The transformation group preserves integral primitive Descartes quadruples

nodes.summary: The transformation group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the Apollonian group together with all $4 \times 4$ permutation matrices.
nodes.title: The transformation group
